items.caption: A modern redraw of 子 in Shang oracle-bone script style. Early forms of 子 depict an infant, fitting its semantic role in 孩, while this image does not show an early form of the full character.
items.alt: A black oracle-script 子 glyph with a rounded upper shape and long lower strokes.
items.selection_reason: Shows the child-related component whose meaning suits 孩; evidence about 子 does not establish an early form or graphic sequence for 孩.

items.caption: A modern redraw of 子 in Western Zhou bronze-script style, illustrating the same child-related component. It is not evidence for the historical form of the full character 孩.
items.alt: A black bronze-script 子 glyph with a rounded loop above branching lower strokes.
items.selection_reason: Provides a visibly distinct script-style example of 子, the component associated with child or infant in 孩.

limitations.text: Both images show 子 rather than 孩. They illustrate a component’s semantic suitability and do not establish an early attestation or the graphic development of 孩.
These are modern redrawings of historical script styles, not photographs of inscribed artifacts.
